The test image shows a whole soybean plant pulled from soil with a notably bleached/pale yellow-white stem, wilted dark leaves still attached, and visible root system. The stem's pale/white coloration is a key feature.

Top candidates: White_Mold (bleached white stems, leaves remain attached), Phytophthora (brown stem from soil line up), Sudden_death_syndrome (white pith, interveinal necrosis).

Let me check reference images across 4 classes.
White Mold reference shows bleached pale stem with black sclerotia. Matches the pale stem in test image. Now checking Phytophthora.
Phytophthora reference shows field-level dying plants, not the bleached stem pattern. Checking Sudden_death_syndrome.
SDS shows field yellowing, not a match. Let me check the White Mold stem/whole plant reference more directly.

This White Mold reference confirms the pattern: bleached/pale stem with black sclerotia. The test image shows the same pale/whitish-bleached stem with wilted dark leaves still attached — classic White Mold presentation.

Key evidence:
- Bleached white/pale yellow stem (hallmark of White Mold)
- Wilted leaves remaining attached to the stem
- Plant pulled from soil showing the full stem
- Matches both White Mold references (bleached stem + black sclerotia pattern)

The other candidates don't fit: Phytophthora shows dark brown discoloration (not bleached white), SDS shows interveinal chlorosis in field canopy, not this single-plant bleached stem presentation.
